pharm: Oxazoline derivative of prednisolone; prodrug converted to active 21-desDFZ; anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressant with claimed lower bone and metabolic impact
summary: Deflazacort is a glucocorticoid and oxazoline derivative of prednisolone, acting as a prodrug for the active metabolite 21-desDFZ. FDA-approved for Duchenne muscular dystrophy in patients aged 2 years and older, dosed at 0.9 mg/kg once daily. It is widely used as a general corticosteroid outside the US and is reported to cause less weight gain and bone loss than prednisone. Long-term therapy must be tapered, not stopped abruptly.
indications: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) in patients 2 years and older (FDA-approved)
General inflammatory and immune-mediated conditions (off-label/non-US use)

dosage.n: Round to nearest possible tablet or suspension dose
Dose to lowest effective level; individualize
Do not stop abruptly; risk of adrenal insufficiency

admin: Take once daily, with or without food
Tablets may be crushed and taken in applesauce
Use supplied dispenser for oral suspension
Do not stop abruptly after long-term use; taper gradually
moa: A prodrug rapidly converted by plasma esterases to the active metabolite 21-desDFZ, which binds glucocorticoid receptors to modulate gene transcription, producing anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressant effects. In DMD the precise mechanism is not fully established.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to deflazacort or any ingredient
relative: Live or live-attenuated vaccines during therapy

preg: May cause fetal harm based on animal data; use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: No human data; other corticosteroids are present in breast milk. Weigh the benefit of breastfeeding against the risk to the infant.

major: Strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, ketoconazole): reduce deflazacort to one-third of the dose
moderate: Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin): reduced deflazacort efficacy
Potassium-depleting agents (diuretics, amphotericin B): risk of hypokalemia
interactions.alcohol: GI ulcer risk; avoid or limit

pk: Not specified (anti-inflammatory effect over hours to days)
Tablets 20–25°C; suspension use within 1 month of opening, do not refrigerate
pearls: Marketed as causing less weight gain and bone loss than prednisone in DMD
Reduce dose to one-third with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors
FDA approval limited to DMD, though used broadly as a general corticosteroid in many countries
missed: Take the dose the same day when remembered; skip if near the next dose. Do not double the dose.
overdose: Chronic overdose causes hypercorticism/Cushingoid features; acute overdose is usually self-limiting. Provide supportive care, monitor electrolytes and glucose, and taper after.
